evals.name: api-names
evals.prompt: Review these proposed names in package dbpool, which exposes Pool as its only constructible type: NewPool, PoolOption, WithTimeout, PoolStatus, MAX_RETRIES, ErrClosed, PoolError. Recommend names at call sites and say which changes would need a migration if already exported.

assertions.text: Recommends dbpool.New and dbpool.Option, avoiding package/type stutter.
Uses MixedCaps for MAX_RETRIES and retains meaningful WithTimeout and ErrClosed conventions.
Recognizes that exported renames can break callers and require migration rather than treating them as automatically safe.
Recommends dbpool.Status instead of PoolStatus and gives a nonstuttering Error-suffixed name for PoolError.
Identifies concrete exported renames needing migration and a compatible transition such as deprecated wrappers or aliases, not only a generic breaking-change warning.

evals.name: boolean-policy
evals.prompt: Our Go repository uses ready bool, Ready() bool, and error text "invalid URL". A reviewer says all three violate Go and demands isReady, IsReady and "invalid url". Resolve the review and explain whether these changes are required.

assertions.text: Accepts ready and Ready under the existing repository convention rather than enforcing mandatory prefixes.
Accepts URL casing in ordinary error prose rather than declaring fully lowercase acronyms mandatory.
Distinguishes optional style policy from language or correctness requirements.
Explains that renaming exported Ready can break callers or interface satisfaction.

evals.name: short-circuit
evals.prompt: Review for readability and show a safe simplification if useful: if user != nil && (user.IsAdmin || expensivePermissionCheck(user)) { allow() }. A teammate wants isAdmin := user.IsAdmin and hasPermission := expensivePermissionCheck(user) computed above the if. The permission check increments an audit counter.

assertions.text: Rejects dereferencing user before its nil guard.
Preserves skipping the permission check for nil users and admins, including its audit side effect.
Does not impose condition extraction merely to meet an operand-count threshold.
Any proposed rewrite evaluates permission exactly once only for non-nil non-admins, and preserves allow outcomes for both true and false permission results.

evals.name: collections
evals.prompt: A Go style patch replaces var users []User with users := []User{} everywhere and var cache map[string]User with cache := map[string]User{} everywhere. One endpoint promises JSON null for absent users; another promises []; cache is read before optional initialization and assignment. Review the policy.

assertions.text: Preserves JSON null for the absent-users contract and requires an empty nonnil slice where [] is promised.
Explains that nil slices support append and need not universally be initialized.
Distinguishes safe nil-map reads from assignments that require initialization.
Explains that eager map allocation removes cache == nil state and may bypass optional or lazy initialization.

evals.name: imports-and-tests
evals.prompt: Review Go names: user_handler_linux_test.go, package http_test, TestParse_InvalidURL, subtest "invalid URL", import apiv1 "example.com/api/v1" and apiv2 "example.com/api/v2" (both declare package api), and f "fmt". Which should change and why?

assertions.text: Accepts file/test suffixes, external test package underscore and test subcase underscore.
Judges apiv1/apiv2 by the declared package api collision, not by import path suffixes.
Removes gratuitous f alias and does not mandate lowercasing URL in the subtest.

evals.name: enum-and-options
evals.source: golang-naming: enums and options; approved corrections
evals.prompt: Package retry uses type Mode int with ModeAutomatic at zero intentionally meaning the default behavior, ModeDisabled at one, and Option func(*Client) with WithBackoff. It already has Retry and RetryContext. A reviewer requires ModeUnknown at zero, ClientOption and RetryWithContext. Review those requirements.

assertions.text: Preserves the intentionally useful zero value rather than inserting an obligatory unknown sentinel.
Accepts retry.Option and WithBackoff without adding redundant Client qualification.
Accepts the established Context suffix rather than requiring WithContext or renaming an existing API.
Preserves ModeDisabled at one and explains the behavioral or compatibility consequence of shifting existing enum values.

evals.name: pointer-and-layout
evals.prompt: Review the claim: every struct over 128 bytes must be passed by pointer for speed, even read-only ones, and every four-argument Go call must wrap. Our published function signature has five parameters; callers rely on it. Recommend a style policy.

assertions.text: Treats 128 bytes as a heuristic and calls for measurement before performance claims.
Treats call wrapping as readability judgment instead of an unconditional argument-count rule.
Acknowledges public signature compatibility before proposing parameter grouping.

evals.name: returns-and-priority
evals.source: golang-code-style: control flow and named returns
evals.prompt: Review a proposed Go cleanup: a function with named err and defer func(){ err = errors.Join(err, closeFile()) }() should lose its named return; and switch {case debug: level=Debug; case verbose: level=Warn} should become two independent ifs in that order. Both debug and verbose can be true. Explain any behavior risk and suggest a safe form.

assertions.text: Preserves the deferred modification of the returned error rather than blindly removing its named result.
Preserves debug precedence when debug and verbose are both true.
Provides or describes a safe switch or mutually exclusive branching alternative.
Retains deferred cleanup or, if suggesting normal-return cleanup instead, explains the lost panic-unwinding cleanup and provides a way to preserve it.

evals.name: explicit-style-request
evals.prompt: For a teaching slide, show one Go call send(ctx, userID, message, priority) on a single line. Then explain the usual readability convention in one sentence. Do not redesign send.

assertions.text: Honors the explicit single-line request rather than enforcing one argument per line.
Does not change send signature or introduce an options struct.
Gives the requested one-sentence explanation about call layout or line wrapping and readability, rather than only argument naming/order.

evals.name: variant-names
evals.prompt: Our Go slice package already uses SortInPlace and ReverseInPlace for mutation and ParseConfig for an error-returning parser. A proposal would rename the first two to SortIn and ReverseIn because Go requires In, and add a panic-on-error parser and format-string error wrapper. Review and name the new variants.

assertions.text: Rejects In as a universal requirement and preserves the established InPlace convention.
Uses MustParseConfig or equivalent Must-prefixed panic variant.
Uses an f-suffixed formatting wrapper such as Wrapf distinct from plain-message functions.

evals.name: lazy-map-style
evals.prompt: Review this Go style cleanup. Existing code: var limits map[string]int; if limits == nil { limits = loadDefaults() }; limits["max"] = 5. loadDefaults returns a nonnil map containing other required keys. The patch only changes the declaration to limits := map[string]int{}. Is that a harmless clarity improvement? Explain a safe choice.

assertions.text: Rejects the patch because it prevents loadDefaults from running and loses its other required keys.
Preserves the lazy initialization or calls loadDefaults explicitly before assignment rather than replacing it with an empty map.
Distinguishes an empty nonnil map from nil without claiming that nil map reads panic.

evals.name: cleanup-style
evals.prompt: A Go style review wants to shorten this function by removing defer and calling release() just before return, because doTask() has only one explicit return path: func run() (err error) { acquire(); defer release(); return doTask() }. doTask may panic and a caller recovers. Review the change and suggest the smallest safe cleanup; release must run exactly once after acquire succeeds.

assertions.text: Rejects moving release only onto the normal-return path because it would be skipped during panic unwinding.
Preserves exactly-once deferred release after successful acquire, including on panic, without swallowing the panic.
Recognizes the named err is unnecessary here because the defer does not modify it, so an unnamed error result is a safe optional simplification.
